writeup: TIC 65051771 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 6.21 percent and an orbital period of 4.2494 days. A secondary eclipse was detected at 5.4 sigma significance near orbital phase 0.48, consistent with a close binary system. The Box Least Squares search algorithm identified this candidate with a signal-to-noise ratio of 152.6, and pixel-level image analysis using difference imaging confirmed the source at a peak signal-to-noise of 43.6 with a centroid offset of 2.1 arcseconds from the target position. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel target for potential follow-up observations.
